title: PINIR: A Physics-Informed Near-Infrared Framework for Vehicle-Mounted Road Surface Classification
content:
Direct force-based measurements of road–tire friction cannot be performed continuously 1
ahead of a moving vehicle. Road surface condition classification therefore provides an 2
important surrogate for identifying surfaces associated with potentially hazardous driving 3
conditions. This paper introduces the Physics-Informed Near-Infrared Road Surface Classi- 4
fication (PINIR) Framework, which formulates vehicle-mounted road surface classification 5
as a physics-informed optical information-processing problem. 6
The framework combines active near-infrared measurements at 980nm, 1310nm 7
and 1550nm with relative spectral calibration, reference-controlled adaptive temporal 8
filtering, a physically motivated optical representation and a fixed-centroid decision rule. 9
The representation combines wavelength ratios with the total calibrated optical response, 10
retaining information associated with both wavelength-dependent attenuation and surface 11
scattering. 12
The framework was evaluated using 140,165 manually annotated measurements 13
acquired under representative Nordic road conditions. It achieved a four-class accuracy 14
of 87.2% for classification of dry, wet, snow-covered and ice-covered road surfaces. After 15
mapping both the reference labels and predictions to operational groups associated with 16
high and low expected road–tire friction, the accuracy increased to 96.2% . The principal 17
four-class errors occurred between snow and ice, while the main cross-group error was the 18
classification of ice as wet asphalt. 19
The results indicate that physically motivated optical representations can provide 20
strong road surface classification performance using a deterministic and traceable decision 21
process. The proposed PINIR Framework thereby provides an interpretable alternative to 22
approaches based on statistically learned feature representations.
